summary: What worked: two cheap, single-constant changes. (1) TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 (grad_accum 2 -> 1, LRs unchanged): 1.012347 -> 1.003678, which became the base for the whole cell. (2) A wider MLP, MLP_RATIO 4 -> 6 (hidden 2048 -> 3072): 1.003678 -> 0.989682, the largest single effect measured here; the curve is monotone 3 (1.0097) < 4 (1.0037) < 6 (0.9897) and then plateaus at 9 (0.988276), consistent with the run being launch/memory-bound at ~23% MFU rather than FLOP-bound. Final run: a1's depth-12 base + UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004 -> 0.012 = 0.986119 (cell best, but only -0.0004 vs a1's 0.986500, i.e. within noise). What did not work: MLP_RATIO 3 (1.009719), and, importantly, stacking capacity levers - depth 12 + MLP_RATIO 6 + short window 512 gave 0.987973, worse than depth 12 alone; a2/a4/a1 measured the same saturation from other directions, so wide MLP, shorter windows, more width and more depth are all buying the same saturated per-step capacity. What I would try next: non-capacity levers, since capacity is saturated near 0.986 - confirm and tune the unembedding/embedding LRs (0.008-0.02) with repeats to beat noise, the warmdown shape (WARMDOWN_RATIO/FINAL_LR_FRAC, untouched by anyone), and data efficiency, since runs already reach epoch 1 and repeat data inside 5 minutes.
